title: Elastic Batch Shaper & Attention-Aware Kernel Profiler to Reduce Decode Tail Latency
creator: Nadia Patel
description: Context: Production traffic shows persistent 95th/99th token-latency spikes for mixed-length streaming workloads. Root analysis points to two correlated causes: (1) suboptimal kernel selection when batches contain heterogeneous sequence-lengths + attention patterns, and (2) rigid batch cutoffs that allow a few long requests to inflate overall tail latency. Goal: deliver a low-risk runtime change that reduces decode tail latency for mixed workloads without regressing median latency or throughput. Scope: implement an elastic batch shaper (a runtime admission modifier that gently reshapes windows using fast heuristics) + an attention-aware kernel profiler that influences scheduling and batch composition. Constraints: maintain backward-compatible API, no per-request blocking on heavyweight profiling, and keep overhead < 1% p99 cpu/gpu time on steady-state traffic.
background: We already have continuous batching and prefill/decode separation in the runtime. Recent incidents and passive telemetry (trace sampling + kernel timings) show situations where a few long-sequence requests pull preferred kernel selection toward long-seq kernels, producing inefficient paths for the majority of short requests. Existing admission heuristics are static (time-window or fixed token counts) and do not account for attention pattern complexity. Prior tickets (ENG-62341, ENG-70012) targeted prefill gating and window stabilizers but did not address kernel misclassification or elastic window adjustments tied to attention costs.
proposal_summary: 1) Elastic Batch Shaper: at the admission layer, compute a lightweight per-request shape score (sequence length, estimated KV size, presence of cross-attention patterns) and maintain a short-lived reservoir of recent shape statistics. Use that reservoir to adaptively weight how long to keep an admission window open and when to favor fast-path packing. Introduce soft hedging so a small fraction of threads can start a conservative short-window flush when tails form. 2) Attention-Aware Kernel Profiler: sample ~1% of requests to run a micro-probe that estimates attention matrix density and memory pressure (cheap ops on CPU/GPU). Feed profiling signals to the kernel selector to prefer compact kernels for high-density attention cases and alternate kernels for sparse attention. 3) Graceful decode fallback: add a fast path that can preemptively switch to a lower-latency kernel for the current batch if the runtime detects a rising latency gradient. This fallback must be non-blocking and revert when the gradient subsides.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-token latency reduced by >=20% on mixed-length synthetic workload (mix: 60% short <64, 30% mid 64-512, 10% long >512) compared to baseline
No more than 2% regression in median token latency across representative steady-state traces
CPU/GPU overhead of profiling <1% at 1% sampling rate
No feature/regression test failures and integration test coverage for shaper heuristics
Ship with runtime toggle flags and rollout plan (canary -> 50% -> 100%)
implementation_notes: Week 1: instrumentation and lightweight shape score; add reservoir metrics to /metrics and tracing
Week 2: implement elastic window controller and soft-hedge workers; add unit tests for window behavior
Week 3: attention micro-probe + kernel selector integration; end-to-end perf harness against replay traces
Week 4: canary rollout, observe p50/p95/p99, iterate heuristics, prepare rollout runbook
risks: Profiling noise: micro-probe may mis-estimate attention on heavily-quantized models
Overfitting heuristics to synthetic traffic; may cause oscillation under real-world bursts
Compatibility: certain custom kernels may not expose the signals we need; add fallbacks
test_plan: Synthetic workload suite with configurable mixes (short/mid/long) run in CI perf lane
Replay real production traces (sanitized) in a staging cluster to validate tail behavior
A/B canary measuring p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization and token throughput; automated rollback on defined regressions
Unit tests for reservoir statistics and deterministic window transitions
notes: Spoke with infra (Priya Khanna) about exposing lightweight GPU-side counters — agreed to a minimal set to keep overhead low (L2 cache miss proxy, active-kv-size estimate)
Design review scheduled 2026-02-26; PM feedback: require rollout kill-switch and customer opt-out flag for Dedicated tenants
Requested sample traces from a top enterprise customer for validation — legal review pending
